topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: LEO satellites' smaller beam sizes reduce interference, increasing capacity. Adaptive beam design is crucial to maintain coverage, considering differential delay in PHY and MAC procedures. Phased array antennas enable electronic beam steering, but introduce sidelobes, affecting gain and portability trade-offs.
reference_context: SatCom systems involve LEO and GEO satellites with different transmission models, beam sizes, and fading channels, impacting antenna design and gain optimization.
